mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly expresses the qualitative statement of the second law of thermodynamics?

options.A: Heat can be completely converted into work without any other effect.
options.B: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
options.C: Energy can be created or destroyed.

mcqs.answer: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
mcqs.explanation: The second law states that in an isolated system heat flows spontaneously from higher to lower temperature; it cannot flow from cold to hot without external work. Option B captures this qualitative statement. Options A and C contradict the first law, and D is false because many natural processes are irreversible.

mcqs.question: Two metal blocks, one at 80 °C and the other at 30 °C, are placed in thermal contact and insulated from the surroundings. In which direction will heat flow spontaneously?

options.A: From the 30 °C block to the 80 °C block
options.B: From the 80 °C block to the 30 °C block
options.C: No net heat flow will occur
options.D: Heat will flow alternately back and forth

mcqs.answer: From the 80 °C block to the 30 °C block
mcqs.explanation: According to the second law, heat flows spontaneously from a higher‑temperature body to a lower‑temperature body. Hence heat moves from 80 °C to 30 °C. Options A, C, and D contradict this natural direction.

mcqs.question: A heat engine operates between a source at 500 K and a sink at 300 K. Which statement correctly reflects the limitation imposed by the second law on its efficiency?

options.A: Its efficiency can be 100 % if the engine is ideal.
options.B: Its efficiency can exceed that of a Carnot engine.
options.D: Its efficiency is independent of the temperatures of source and sink.

mcqs.explanation: The Carnot efficiency for a reversible engine between 500 K and 300 K is 1 – Tc/Th = 0.40 (40 %). No real or ideal engine can surpass this limit. Options A and B violate the second law, and D ignores the temperature dependence.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: A gas expands slowly against a piston with an infinitesimal pressure difference and is later compressed back to its original state by exactly reversing the steps. In another case, the same gas expands freely into a vacuum and is then compressed back by applying external pressure. Which of the following describes the reversible process?

options.A: The slow expansion and compression (quasi‑static) process
options.B: The free expansion and subsequent compression process

mcqs.answer: The slow expansion and compression (quasi‑static) process
mcqs.explanation: A reversible process must be quasi‑static and generate no entropy; the slow, infinitesimal‑difference expansion/compression meets this criterion. Free expansion is highly irreversible because it creates entropy, and the subsequent compression cannot retrace the original path.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about the second law of thermodynamics?

options.A: The second law allows the complete conversion of heat from a reservoir into work without any other effect.
options.B: The second law forbids 100 % conversion of heat into work in a cyclic process.
options.C: Entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
options.D: Heat naturally flows from a hotter to a colder body.

mcqs.answer: The second law allows the complete conversion of heat from a reservoir into work without any other effect.
mcqs.explanation: Option A is a misconception; the second law explicitly states that it is impossible to convert all the heat from a single reservoir into work in a cyclic process. Options B, C, and D are correct statements of the law.

mcqs.question: Why does heat not flow spontaneously from a colder body to a hotter body?

options.A: Because the entropy of the colder body would increase.
options.B: Because such a flow would decrease the total entropy of the isolated system.
options.C: Because temperature is not related to entropy.
options.D: Because heat cannot be transferred between bodies.

mcqs.answer: Because such a flow would decrease the total entropy of the isolated system.
mcqs.explanation: Spontaneous processes in an isolated system must increase total entropy. Heat flowing from cold to hot would reduce the overall entropy, violating the second law. Option A is irrelevant, C is false, and D is incorrect because heat transfer is possible.

mcqs.question: Consider a Carnot engine and a real engine both operating between the same high temperature Th and low temperature Tl. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Both engines have the same efficiency because efficiency depends only on Th and Tl.
options.B: The Carnot engine has higher efficiency than the real engine because it is reversible.
options.C: The real engine can have higher efficiency than the Carnot engine if friction is minimized.
options.D: Both engines can achieve 100 % efficiency if Th is much greater than Tl.

mcqs.answer: The Carnot engine has higher efficiency than the real engine because it is reversible.
mcqs.explanation: The Carnot engine represents the maximum possible efficiency for given Th and Tl and is reversible. Real engines suffer irreversibilities (friction, heat losses) and therefore have lower efficiency. Options A, C, and D contradict the second law and the definition of Carnot efficiency.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: An ideal gas undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion from volume V₁ to V₂ at temperature T, followed by an irreversible adiabatic expansion to volume V₃. Which of the following correctly describes the net entropy change of the gas for the whole process?
mcqs.explanation: During the reversible isothermal expansion the entropy increase is nR ln(V₂/V₁). The subsequent irreversible adiabatic expansion generates additional entropy (since it is irreversible) even though no heat is exchanged. Therefore the total entropy change is greater than the isothermal contribution alone, making option C correct. Options A and B ignore the entropy generated in the irreversible step, and D is impossible for an isolated adiabatic irreversible expansion.
